method_note: CoRL 2026 (Austin, 9–12 Nov 2026) has not yet taken place, so CoRL 2025 (Seoul, 27–30 Sep 2025) is analyzed. The official main-conference program lists 263 papers: 42 in 6 titled oral sessions (Manipulation I, Perception, Manipulation II, Planning & Safety & Robustness, Locomotion, Humanoid & Hardware) and 221 in 6 untitled Spotlight sessions, so session titles cover only 16% of papers. OpenReview keyword/area metadata could not be retrieved (API returned a bot-challenge), so every paper TITLE was classified with a documented, priority-ordered regex rule set (domain terms such as medical, UAV, driving, humanoid/legged/locomotion, multi-robot, HRI/teleoperation, manipulation/grasp/dexterous first; then VLA/VLM/LLM/language → foundation-models; SLAM/localization; perception/vision/3D/tactile; planning/navigation/trajectory; MPC/safety → control-theory; then generic learning terms → robot-learning). A paper takes its first 1–2 matching ids (0.5 each if 2); 18 papers matching no rule were assigned robot-learning (CoRL's scope). Weight = paper-equivalents / 263; ids below 0.02 omitted (multi-robot, autonomous-vehicles, uav, slam, mechanisms, field-robotics, medical-robotics total ~0.055). Title-based coding is heuristic and is the dataset author's, not CoRL's.
